value.overview: The Masked Duck is a small, secretive diving duck of tropical wetlands in the Americas. It is the only species in the genus Nomonyx and is related to the stiff-tailed ducks. Usually found alone or in pairs, it spends much of the day hidden among aquatic vegetation and often feeds at dusk or during the night. In Costa Rica it is an uncommon, local duck found in suitable freshwater wetlands from lowlands to middle elevations.
value.classification: The Masked Duck belongs to the order Anseriformes and family Anatidae. It is the sole species in the genus Nomonyx.
value.identification: This compact duck has a short, sturdy body and a pointed tail that is often held upright. The breeding-plumaged male has a dark rusty-brown body, a black facial mask, pale cheek markings, and a striking blue bill. Females and immature birds are more frequently observed and have a brown body, a buff-colored face, and two dark facial stripes. The species is usually recognized by its small size, secretive behavior, and preference for dense marsh vegetation.
value.rangeHabitat: The Masked Duck ranges through tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas, including Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and much of northern and central South America. In Costa Rica it is an uncommon and local resident, recorded especially in the Central Valley around Cartago, the Tempisque basin of Guanacaste, the Río Frío region, and other lowland and middle-elevation areas. It favors shallow freshwater ponds, marshes, quiet lagoons, flooded fields, roadside ditches, and wetlands with abundant emergent vegetation.
value.migrationStatus: In Costa Rica, the Masked Duck is generally considered a local resident rather than a regular long-distance migrant. It may make short-distance movements in response to water levels and wetland conditions, and its numbers and detectability can vary seasonally.
value.breeding: The Masked Duck breeds in freshwater marshes, ponds, and lagoons with dense floating or emergent vegetation. The nest is usually a shallow structure concealed among aquatic plants, and the female raises the young with limited or no assistance from the male. Breeding in Costa Rica has been reported mainly during the wet season, when water levels and aquatic vegetation provide suitable nesting and feeding conditions. The species is secretive during breeding and can be difficult to survey accurately.
value.dietFeeding: It feeds mainly by diving in shallow water, taking aquatic invertebrates, seeds, aquatic plants, and other small wetland organisms. Feeding often occurs at dusk or after dark, which contributes to the species’ low visibility. The Masked Duck may remain underwater for considerable periods and commonly forages in quiet ponds or marshes rather than in large open lakes. It usually rests during the day among dense vegetation.
value.behavior: The Masked Duck is shy and easily overlooked. It often rests motionless in marsh vegetation, swims quietly, and dives when approached instead of flying immediately. When flushed, it can spring directly into the air from the water. Birds are commonly solitary or occur in small groups. Males may display the raised tail typical of stiff-tailed ducks, while females and immature birds generally provide the majority of sightings because they are less conspicuous in appearance.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population trend is not reliably quantified; available assessments do not identify the species as globally threatened.
